library(fontawesome)

Haptic feedback is indispensable to our everyday tasks, from tapping on a smartphone to crafting woodwork.
Such an essential sense, however, is limited to vibrotactile feedback in most VR experiences, usually enabled by hand-held controllers.
Although many researchers have designed haptic devices in the field of HCI and VR, they often focus on the hands.
We aim to enable haptic input and output through Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) to explore haptic feedback on the face.

# FacePush
Creating haptic feedback on face through a pulley system using motors install on the VR HMD.

[`r fa("book")` UIST '18](https://doi.org/10.1145/3242587.3242588)
[`r fa("youtube")`](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IPLVCdbvWyI)

# FaceWidgets
Installing physical controls, such as buttons and joysticks, on the HMD to support tangible input in VR.

[`r fa("book")` UIST '19](https://doi.org/10.1145/3332165.3347946)
[`r fa("youtube")`](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e_Bty05zuAc)

# Skin-Stroke Display
Demonstrating skin-stroke feedback on face while using VR HMDs.

[`r fa("book")` CHI '20](https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376700)
[`r fa("youtube")`](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_UXC9lZF0)
